info.title: Linkly
info.description: Linkly is a link shortener and click tracker. Create branded short links with custom domains, add UTM parameters and retargeting pixels, report conversions, and pull click analytics grouped by country, platform, referrer or campaign.

get.description: Returns the most recent conversions recorded in the workspace.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of conversions to return, between 1 and 1000.

amount_cents.description: The value in the smallest currency unit. May be negative to record a refund.

click_id.description: The ID of the attributed click.

country.description: A two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code, for example US.

currency.description: The ISO 4217 currency code. Defaults to USD.

event_id.description: Your identifier for the event. Reporting the same value twice does not create a second conversion.

event_name.description: What happened, for example purchase, signup or trial_started.

event_type.description: The coarse event type. Use lead to establish customer identity and sale to record revenue. Defaults to custom.

external_id.description: Your identifier for the customer. Send it on every event so later sales can be linked to the original click.

id.description: The unique identifier of the conversion. IDs sort chronologically.

ip_source.description: Whose address was recorded: visitor, server or unknown. Server means the connecting address belonged to your backend or a platform relay, so it is excluded from geographic reporting.

link_id.description: The ID of the attributed link, or null if the conversion could not be attributed to a link.

metadata.description: Arbitrary JSON metadata, up to 10,000 bytes.

occurred_at.description: When the conversion happened, in ISO 8601 format. Defaults to now.

post.description: Records a conversion such as a purchase, sign-up or custom event, and attributes it to the link that was clicked when an attribution token is supplied.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: The conversion to record.

amount_cents.description: Value in the smallest currency unit. May be negative to record a refund or chargeback, which nets against earlier revenue.

country.description: Two-letter country code for the conversion. Inferred for browser-side calls; supply it explicitly from a server-side integration, where the connecting address is your own infrastructure rather than the customer's.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code. Defaults to USD.

event_id.description: Your identifier for this event. Used as an idempotency key; reporting the same value twice will not create a second conversion. Applies to any event type, not just purchases.

event_name.description: What happened, e.g. purchase, signup, trial_started.

event_type.description: Coarse type driving the funnel. lead establishes customer identity, sale records revenue. Defaults to custom.

external_id.description: Your identifier for the customer. Send it on every event: it is what links a later server-side sale back to the click that produced the signup.

linkly_cid.description: The attribution token captured from the landing page URL. Omit if unavailable; the conversion is then recorded without a link attribution.

metadata.description: Arbitrary JSON, up to 10,000 bytes encoded.

occurred_at.description: When the conversion happened. Defaults to now.

visitor_ip.description: The end customer's IP, when your server has it. Omit unless you do; for server-side calls Linkly otherwise records the connecting address as your server, not the customer, and excludes it from geographic reporting. Sending this asserts you have a lawful basis to share it. Never returned by the API.

200.description: The recorded conversion. If the event ID was already reported, the existing conversion is returned.

post.description: Creates a new short link, or updates an existing one when a link ID is supplied. Supports custom domains and slugs, UTM parameters, retargeting pixels and Open Graph metadata.

get.description: Returns click counts over time for a workspace or for specific links, optionally filtered by date range, country, browser, platform, referrer or ISP.

parameters.name: workspace_id
parameters.description: The workspace to work in. Choose it from the list, or enter its ID.

parameters.name: link_id
parameters.description: The ID of a single link to filter by.

parameters.name: link_ids
parameters.description: A hyphen-separated list of link IDs to filter by.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: The start of the date range, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: The end of the date range, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: A two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code, for example US.

parameters.name: browser
parameters.description: A browser name to filter by, for example Chrome, Firefox or Safari.

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: A platform or operating system to filter by, for example Windows, Mac, iOS or Android.

parameters.name: referer
parameters.description: A referring domain to filter by.

parameters.name: isp
parameters.description: An internet service provider name to filter by.

parameters.name: bots
parameters.description: Whether to include clicks identified as bots. Set to false to exclude them.

parameters.name: unique
parameters.description: Whether to count only unique clicks.

parameters.name: timezone
parameters.description: The IANA time zone used for date calculations, for example Europe/London.

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.description: The granularity of the time series, either day or hour.

t.description: The bucket start: YYYY-MM-DD for daily buckets or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS for hourly buckets.

y.description: The number of clicks in the bucket.

get.description: Returns click counts grouped by a dimension such as country, city, platform, referrer or UTM parameter, ordered by count descending.

parameters.name: workspace_id
parameters.description: The workspace to work in. Choose it from the list, or enter its ID.

parameters.name: counter
parameters.description: The dimension to group clicks by, for example country, city, platform, referer or utm_campaign.

parameters.name: link_id
parameters.description: The ID of a single link to filter by.

parameters.name: link_ids
parameters.description: A hyphen-separated list of link IDs to filter by.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: The start of the date range, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: The end of the date range, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: A two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code, for example US.

parameters.name: bots
parameters.description: Whether to include clicks identified as bots. Set to false to exclude them.

parameters.name: unique
parameters.description: Whether to count only unique clicks.

total.description: Total clicks across all groups, including any not returned in values. When the result is truncated this is greater than the sum of count in values, so count / total still gives an accurate percentage.

values.description: Grouped counts, ordered by count descending. Truncated to the top 10,000 values; if the dimension has more distinct values than that, the rest are not returned.

count.description: The number of clicks for this value.

value.description: The value of the dimension, for example a country code.

parameters.description: The page number to return, starting at 1.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: The number of links to return per page.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: The field to sort by, for example clicks_total, name or inserted_at.

parameters.name: sort_dir
parameters.description: The sort direction, either asc or desc.

parameters.name: deleted
parameters.description: Whether to return links that are in the trash instead of active links.
